CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, persistent fatigue, sleep quality, and headache frequency.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment following the changes made to his treatment regimen last month. He reports that the addition of Melatonin 5 mg nightly has resulted in a notable improvement in his sleep quality. Mr. Smith states that he is now averaging six to seven hours of sleep per night, with fewer awakenings throughout the night. He describes his sleep as more restorative, although he still experiences occasional difficulty falling asleep on particularly stressful nights.
Despite these improvements, Mr. Smith continues to express concerns regarding his persistent fatigue, which he attributes to both his ongoing anxiety and his previous history of obstructive sleep apnea. He notes that while his daytime drowsiness has decreased somewhat, he still feels fatigued in the afternoons, particularly after a night of disrupted sleep.
Regarding his headaches, Mr. Smith reports that the frequency has remained stable at four episodes per week, but he has experienced a slight increase in intensity over the past week. He continues to use Ibuprofen as needed, taking it approximately three times a week, but has noted that it provides only partial relief. He describes the headaches as bilateral and throbbing, often exacerbated by stress and lack of sleep.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General: Persistent fatigue; reports slight weight gain of 2 lbs over the past month. Cardiovascular: Intermittent palpitations stable; denies chest pain or edema. Respiratory: No shortness of breath; CPAP compliance reported, no cough or wheezing. Gastrointestinal: Mild nausea persists; occasional bloating; no vomiting or changes in bowel habits. Neurological: Increased headache intensity; no focal neurological deficits.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Mild obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed on sleep study. - Tension-type headaches.
FAMILY HISTORY
- Father: Coronary artery disease, underwent CABG at age 60. - Mother: Hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
- Lives alone in , . Works as a teacher. No tobacco use; social alcohol consumption. No illicit drug use.
MEDICATIONS
- Atorvastatin 10 mg daily. - Magnesium supplement 400 mg daily. - Melatonin 5 mg nightly. - Escitalopram 30 mg daily. - Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly. - CPAP machine for sleep apnea.
ALLERGIES
- No known drug allergies.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
VITALS: T 98.4F, HR 76 bpm, BP 122/78 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, O2 sat 95% on room air.
General: Well-nourished, alert, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. No peripheral edema. Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally; CPAP device noted, no wheezing or crackles. Gastrointestinal: Soft, non-tender abdomen; no epigastric tenderness. Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no focal deficits. Moderate tenderness noted on palpation of the bilateral temporalis region.
LABORATORY DATA
Lipid Panel (obtained at last visit): Total Cholesterol 158 mg/dL, LDL 78 mg/dL, HDL 60 mg/dL, Triglycerides 82 mg/dL CBC: Normal BMP: Normal TSH: Normal
RADIOLOGICAL STUDIES
- No new studies indicated at this visit.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Persistent fatigue and sleep disturbances with ongoing anxiety. - Mr. Smith reports improved sleep quality with Melatonin but continues to experience fatigue. We will maintain the current regimen of Melatonin 5 mg nightly and Escitalopram 30 mg daily. Consider increasing Amitriptyline to 15 mg nightly if headaches persist and sleep quality does not improve. Reassess CPAP therapy efficacy and consider a follow-up sleep study if symptoms do not improve. Encourage continued adherence to sleep hygiene practices and gradual exercise. Schedule follow-up in 4 weeks to monitor progress.
2. Stable frequency and increased intensity of tension-type headaches. - The patient reports stable headache frequency but increased intensity. Continue Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly; discuss the option of increasing the dose to 15 mg nightly if headaches worsen. Follow-up in 4 weeks to reassess headache frequency and severity.
3. Lipid management. - Continue Atorvastatin 10 mg daily as lipid levels remain stable. Reassess lipid panel in 3 months to evaluate ongoing effectiveness.
4. Follow-up. - Schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks to reassess anxiety symptoms, sleep quality, headache frequency, and overall well-being. Discuss potential referrals for cognitive-behavioral therapy if anxiety symptoms persist or worsen.
